text.p: Spanish government bonds eased with other European markets on Monday, and although dealings were calm analysts said the market was nervous against the background of thin summer holiday trade and the latent threat of profit-taking.

"The market is calm. There are people who are on vacations and a large number of reports expected from the U.S. (this week) will keep the market's attention," said Juan Antonio Mielgo, Bank of America economist in Madrid.
Second-quarter employment cost index and July consumer confidence lead off the week's U.S. data on Tuesday.

Domestically, the next major event is likely to take place on Friday, when the government is expected to release the general guidelines of the 1998 budget. The budget draft must be officially presented to parliament by the end of September.
The market is, however, generally familiar with the government's policy of austerity and is not likely to be affected by the news.
"The government's (budget) guidelines have largely been taken on board by the market," another Madrid-based analyst said.
More worrying is the overhanging threat of profit-taking.
Many are holding on to the market with unrealised profits, and there are suppressed worries that nervous and thin market conditions could lead to declines.
"I think the market looks worrying," the analyst said. "The market is nervous. There are a lot of profits to be realised."
